concepts.title: The Constituent Assembly
concepts.definition: The Constituent Assembly, indirectly elected under the 1946 cabinet mission plan, held its first meeting in December 1946, worked through committees and drafts, and adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, a framing effort of about three years amid partition and refugee crisis.
concepts.key_idea: Partition shadowed every debate: the assembly wrote a constitution for a country bleeding at its borders. Subtracting the first meeting year from the adoption year gives the framing span in years.

concepts.title: Objectives Resolution and Rights
concepts.definition: Nehru's Objectives Resolution of December 1946 promised justice, equality and freedom, and suffrage to all adults; the assembly debated fundamental rights, minority protections and the place of the state vis-a-vis religion, embedding rights in the constitution's core.
concepts.key_idea: The resolution was the constitution's moral preamble, later mirrored in the preamble's keywords.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs304.txt Objectives Resolution and fundamental rights debates
question_patterns: state the promises of the Objectives Resolution
when did Nehru move the resolution

solution_steps.explain: justice social, economic and political; equality of status and opportunity
the adopted preamble echoes the resolution's vocabulary
fundamental rights constitutionalised the freedom struggle's promises

concepts.title: Debates: Language, Federalism, Electorate
concepts.section: The Dominant Voices and the Debates
concepts.definition: Assembly debates weighed a centralising state against provincial demands, Hindi against regional languages, and separate electorates against common citizenship; the majority chose strong central power, Hindi as official language with transitional English, and reserved seats without separate electorates for depressed classes.
concepts.key_idea: Every choice traded unity against diversity, and the final text balanced them through federal checks and temporary provisions.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs304.txt language, centre-state power and electorate debates
question_patterns: summarise the language debate and its settlement

solution_steps.explain: Hindi became official language with English allowed transitionally
partition anxiety pushed the draft toward strong central emergency powers
reserved seats replaced separate electorates for depressed classes

concepts.title: The Constitution's Vision
concepts.definition: The constitution's vision combined a strong state to correct social wrongs, universal adult franchise in a poor society, and social revolution through law - banning untouchability, promising land reform - while accommodating diversity through federal forms.
concepts.key_idea: Adult franchise was the boldest experiment: a largely illiterate nation was trusted to elect its rulers at once.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehs304.txt franchise, social revolution and strong state themes
question_patterns: describe the vision of universal adult franchise

relate the freedom movement's promises to the text
assess the constitution's accommodative design

solution_steps.explain: universal franchise extended power to every adult without property tests
untouchability's abolition aimed at social revolution by statute
federal forms carried diversity while the centre held unity
